matches.rationale: No finding identifies the inflated FT-HID dataset size or the discrepancy between the reported 38,364 samples and the original 9,120 pairs.
Prediction 1 correctly points out that Equation (3) uses (1+cosθ)[u]_x^2, which is an invalid Rodrigues rotation, exactly matching the corruption.
No finding highlights the omission of batch size, warmup, weight decay, or gradient clipping in the training description.
No finding addresses the unfounded 'first egocentric realistic world simulator' claim or ignores prior works like Wonderland and Gen3C.
No finding flags the fabricated 'Matrix-Game [49]' citation or questions its existence.
No finding reveals that evaluation is deceptively limited to indoor scenes, hiding worse outdoor performance.
Prediction 2 identifies the undefined β_t in Equation (1) and the resulting inconsistency with the variance condition, which matches the corruption.
Prediction 8 describes the unfair 'information gap' where PlayerOne receives motion sequences but competitors get only enriched captions, exactly the issue.
No finding challenges the overstatement of 'diverse scenarios' and 'large margins' given the limited 100-video indoor benchmark.
No finding notes the removal of the anonymization statement or the lack of ethical disclosure.
Prediction 11 cites the absolute claim that PlayerOne 'completely solves' the challenge and 'eliminates all limitations,' which is the same rhetorical inflation.
Prediction 3 identifies the contradiction between the abstract's '30 FPS' real-time claim and the actual 8 FPS reported in Section 4.1 and the appendix.
No finding detects the fabricated improvement of PlayerOne's MPJPE to 98.42 in the ablation table or its inconsistency with Table 3.
No finding points out the channel-size mismatch (3 vs. 5) in the motion latent concatenation that would break the DiT input.

Prediction 11 mentions the conclusion's unsupported absolute guarantee of coherent generation 'across all scenarios,' which conflicts with the documented inferior game-scenario performance in the Limitations.
